item.text: {"analysis":"The recency-weighted loss experiment ran successfully but reduced pinned-host macro validation HR@10 to 0.4788, versus the supplied prior score of 0.4913 (−0.0125) and baseline of 0.505 (−0.0262). Category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.500, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.550, Electronics 0.340, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.525. Electronics remains the weakest category. Weighting selected token losses by exp(−distance_from_full_window_endpoint/16), normalized by total weight, did not improve aggregate ranking in this trial. The result does not establish why performance declined; reduced emphasis on earlier transitions is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated cause. Host-reported GPU allocation was 406.845 seconds.","code_summary":"One independently trained ConvRec model and one selected checkpoint per category, with dataset routing and no ensemble. Each network uses 96-dimensional item embeddings, learned item biases, four residual causal convolution blocks with dilations 1/2/4/8, jointly trained two-head causal attention, and final layer normalization over histories of length 64. The isolated change replaces mean cross-entropy with endpoint-relative exponential token weighting. Uniform subsampling up to 2048 tokens, 256 shared uniform negatives, collision masking, optimizer, training schedule, validation checkpoint selection, and inference remain unchanged. Predictor reconstruction strictly loads the selected category checkpoint. Training seed is 42; supplied splits and GAGC_DATA_DIR routing are preserved."}
